q: The Engineer fixes the rate for a substituted item of work under a contract and the contractor disputes the rate so fixed. Where such a matter is listed among the 'excepted matters' of the General Conditions of Contract, the position is that:

options.A: The dispute must be referred to arbitration like any other dispute
options.B: The decision of the Engineer on the matter is final and binding, and it cannot be referred to arbitration
options.C: The tender committee decides the rate afresh
options.D: The contractor may execute the item at his own rate pending settlement

q: A tenderer who has submitted his bid in e-tendering through IREPS asks, after the due date and time for submission have passed but before the tenders are opened, to be allowed to modify the rates in his bid. The request:

options.A: Cannot be entertained, a bid being capable of withdrawal or modification only before the due date and time fixed for its submission
options.B: Can be allowed on payment of a late-modification fee
options.C: Can be allowed with the verbal approval of the tender-opening officer
options.D: Can be allowed if the tenderer is otherwise the lowest bidder

q: Departmental tools and plant are issued to a works contractor on hire under the agreement. On return, a machine is found damaged through the contractor's misuse of it. The cost of making good the damage is:

options.A: Borne by the Railways as a normal maintenance charge of the machine
options.B: Written off against the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Recoverable from the contractor, in addition to the hire charges payable by him for the machine
options.D: Adjusted against the departmental charges of the work

q: In an item-rate contract, the contractor presents a running bill claiming payment for a large quantity of bricks which he has stacked at the site but which have not yet been built into the work. The claim, as payment for work done, is:

options.A: Payable in full, stacking being treated as execution of the item
options.B: Payable at half the item rate as an advance payment
options.C: Payable with the approval of the sectional officer alone
options.D: Not payable as work done, materials not yet incorporated in the work being eligible, if at all, only for a secured advance in accordance with the contract conditions

q: A contractor accepts the final bill of a work in full and final settlement of all his claims, without recording any reservation, and furnishes a no-claim certificate. He thereafter raises a fresh monetary claim in respect of the same contract. Ordinarily, the fresh claim:

options.A: Must be paid, the final bill having no bearing on later claims
options.B: Is not maintainable, the settlement accepted in full and final satisfaction without reservation having closed his claims under the contract
options.C: Can be entertained only by the tender committee
options.D: Is payable from the savings of another work of the division

q: During the execution of a sanctioned work, an additional facility not provided in the sanctioned estimate is ordered to be executed on the verbal instructions of a senior officer, without the prior sanction of a material modification and without finance concurrence. The expenditure so incurred is treated as:

options.A: Unauthorised expenditure, liable to be regularised only under the orders of the competent authority
options.B: A normal variation within the powers of the executing officer
options.C: A charge on the contingencies of the estimate in all cases
options.D: The personal liability of the contractor who executed it

q: The cost of a completed work exceeds its sanctioned estimate by a substantial margin, the excess being wholly due to a rise in the prices of materials and labour, with no change in the scope or design of the work. The excess is regularised by:

options.A: Recovering the excess from the contractor who executed the work
options.B: Writing off the excess against the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Explaining the excess in the completion report/estimate and obtaining the sanction of the competent authority for the revised cost of the work
options.D: Adjusting the excess against the sanctioned estimate of another work having savings

q: A deposit work is in progress and the Railways call upon the outside body to deposit an additional amount, the cost being likely to exceed the amount originally deposited. The body fails to deposit the additional amount. In this position, the Railways should:

options.A: Complete the work in full and recover the excess from the contractor
options.B: Meet the excess from the Railway's own funds as a loan to the body
options.C: Charge the excess to the departmental charges of another deposit work
options.D: Not incur expenditure on the work beyond the amount actually deposited by the body

q: Railway land has been given to a party on licence for a specified purpose. Without obtaining the permission of the Railways, the licensee hands over possession of the land to a third party to use for the same purpose. This act of the licensee:

options.A: Is valid, a licence being freely transferable like a lease
options.B: Is a breach of the licence, a licence being personal to the licensee and not transferable, and renders the licence liable to termination
options.C: Converts the licence into a lease in favour of the third party
options.D: Merely requires an enhancement of the licence fee payable

q: A municipal body constructs a new road which crosses an existing railway line, and asks the Railways to provide and bear the cost of the crossing facilities required by the new road. As a general principle, the cost of the crossing so necessitated is borne by:

options.A: The road authority whose new road has necessitated the crossing
options.B: The Railways, the line being already in existence
options.C: The contractor maintaining the section of the line
options.D: The passengers using the section, through a special cess

q: A contractor's demand for arbitration under a works contract is confined to certain disputes arising out of his final claim. Before the arbitral tribunal, he seeks to introduce an entirely new claim which was never included in his final claim or in his demand for arbitration. The new claim:

options.A: Must be entertained, the tribunal having unlimited jurisdiction over the contract
options.B: Can be entertained with the permission of the Engineer-in-charge
options.C: Cannot be entertained, the reference to arbitration comprising only the disputes in respect of which a demand for arbitration was made, with the claims specified
options.D: Is payable by the Railways if the tribunal finds it genuine, whether demanded or not

q: An arbitral award in a works dispute directs the contractor to pay a sum to the Railways. The award is not challenged within the period allowed and the contractor does not pay. The Railways can recover the amount by:

options.A: Forfeiting the earnest money of all the tenderers of the work
options.B: Deducting it from the wages of the contractor's labour
options.C: Asking the tender committee to pass a recovery order
options.D: Getting the award executed in the same manner as a decree of a civil court

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a toll-based BOT concession, the concessionaire recovers his investment mainly from the user charges collected by him and bears the traffic risk of the project.
2. In an annuity-based concession, the concessionaire is paid fixed annuity amounts by the authority and the traffic risk remains with the authority.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: In an EPC contract, the detailed design prepared by the contractor is examined and approved by the engineer appointed by the authority for the project. A defect in the design comes to light during execution. The responsibility for the defective design rests with:

options.A: The contractor, the approval of his design by the authority's engineer not relieving him of his responsibility for the design
options.B: The authority's engineer alone, his approval having transferred the responsibility
options.C: The tender committee which recommended the award of the contract
options.D: The Railways' Accounts office, which passed the contractor's bills

q: In an EPC contract, the authority requires the contractor to provide an additional facility which lies wholly outside the scope and performance specifications defined in the agreement. Such a requirement is dealt with as:

options.A: Part of the contractor's original obligation within the lump-sum price
options.B: A ground for terminating the contract at the contractor's cost
options.C: A change of scope under the agreement, with its implications for price and time dealt with in accordance with the agreement
options.D: An extra item payable at the schedule of rates in all cases

q: A firm which prepared the Detailed Project Report and the design of a railway project later submits a tender to execute the same work as a contractor. Its participation in the tender is objectionable mainly because:

options.A: A consultant can never become a contractor for any work
options.B: The firm would have to furnish double earnest money
options.C: The firm is not enlisted in any class of contractors
options.D: It creates a conflict of interest, the firm having had access to the project's design and estimates and thereby an unfair advantage over other tenderers

q: At a pre-bid conference for a major work, an important clarification of the tender conditions is agreed upon, and the executive issues it only to the firms which attended the conference. This course is improper because:

options.A: Clarifications can never be issued after the tender notice
options.B: Clarifications and amendments arising out of the pre-bid conference must be issued to all the prospective tenderers, so that all of them bid on the same conditions
options.C: The clarification should have been issued by the Accounts office
options.D: Pre-bid conferences are not permitted for major works

q: On the completion of a work, the sectional engineer assures the contractor that the liquidated damages levied on him for delayed completion will be waived. Such an assurance:

options.A: Cannot bind the Railways, remission or waiver of liquidated damages being a matter for the authority competent under the contract and the delegation of powers, and not for the site officials
options.B: Automatically cancels the liquidated damages recorded in the final bill
options.C: Is valid if it is recorded in the site order book
options.D: Is valid if the contractor has otherwise performed the work well

q: A contractor concretes the foundation of a structure, covering up the reinforcement, without giving the notice required for its inspection and measurement by the Engineer. On this coming to notice, the Engineer may:

options.A: Accept the work on the basis of the contractor's own records
options.B: Certify the concealed work as satisfactory without any check
options.C: Require the work to be opened up for inspection and measurement at the cost of the contractor
options.D: Stop payment of all the bills of the contractor under every contract

q: Cement brought to the site of a work by the contractor is found stored in the open, stacked directly on the ground, exposed to rain. The storage is objectionable and the cement liable to deterioration because cement for the work is required to be stored:

options.A: In the open, so that it remains accessible for inspection
options.B: In the contractor's head office until the day of use
options.C: Only in bags hired from the Railways
options.D: In a dry, weatherproof shed, stacked on a raised platform clear of the ground and the walls

q: A special machine is purchased exclusively for the execution of a particular work and is charged to that work. On completion of the work, the machine is retained by the division as it is expected to be generally useful on other works for several years. In this changed position, the correct accountal is that:

options.A: The full cost of the machine continues to stand charged to the completed work in all cases
options.B: The work is relieved of the value of the machine retained for general use, only the depreciation or hire-equivalent for the period of its use on the work remaining chargeable to the work
options.C: The cost of the machine is recovered from the contractor of the work
options.D: The machine is written off as scrap at the close of the work

q: At the close of a financial year, a portion of a sanctioned work stands executed and measured, but the contractor's bill for it has neither been passed nor paid before 31st March. To bring the liability into the accounts of the year in which the work was actually done, the amount is:

options.A: Debited to the work and credited to Demands Payable
options.B: Kept outside the accounts altogether until the bill is paid in the next year
options.C: Debited to Miscellaneous Works Advances and forgotten thereafter
options.D: Charged to the work of the following year as fresh expenditure

q: A contract is closed while a mobilisation advance paid to the contractor still remains partly unrecovered, no further bills of that contract being due. The outstanding advance is dealt with by:

options.A: Writing it off automatically at the close of the contract
options.B: Adjusting it against the earnest money of the unsuccessful tenderers
options.C: Recovering it from the sums due to the contractor under other contracts or from his securities, and holding it under a suspense head such as Miscellaneous Works Advances until it is recovered
options.D: Charging it to the departmental charges of the work

q: A number of limited height subways at level crossings in a section are sanctioned together as one umbrella work. Before one of the subways covered by the umbrella is actually taken up for execution, it is necessary that:

options.A: Its detailed estimate is sanctioned by the competent authority and funds are allotted for it under the umbrella work
options.B: A separate entry is made for it in the Pink Book as an independent itemised work
options.C: The sanction of the Railway Board is obtained afresh for each subway
options.D: A separate tender committee is constituted by the Railway Board for it

q: Against a sanctioned work, only a token provision has been made in the budget of the year. The executive proposes to incur expenditure on the work during the year far in excess of the amount so allotted, expecting a larger allotment in the next year. The proposal is not in order because:

options.A: A token provision means that the work has been dropped altogether
options.B: Expenditure on the work in the year can be incurred only after the completion report is sanctioned
options.C: The work can be executed only through a deposit from an outside body
options.D: Expenditure on a work in a year must be kept within the allotment actually made for it for that year, a token provision supporting only a nominal outlay in that year

q: A contractor's running bill for a work is passed for payment and the Accounts office releases the net amount after deducting tax at source on the gross amount payable. Such deduction from contractors' bills is made in accordance with:

options.A: The provisions of the Income-tax Act relating to tax deducted at source
options.B: The orders of the Tender Committee which accepted the tender
options.C: A condition in the Measurement Book under which the bill is prepared
options.D: The Schedule of Powers of the accepting authority

q: The completion report of a finished work is sent to the Accounts office for verification. In the course of such verification, Accounts primarily satisfies itself that:

options.A: The contractor has been enlisted in the appropriate class for future works
options.B: The final expenditure agrees with the sanctioned estimate, the works register and the final bill, and variations are properly explained
options.C: The asset created by the work has been entered in the Pink Book of the next year
options.D: The performance guarantee of the contractor has been converted into security deposit

q: During a budgetary review, the executive finds that a sanctioned work will cost much less than the allotment provided for it in the year and that the surplus funds are not required for that work. The correct treatment of the anticipated saving is that it should be:

options.A: Retained informally by the division for any petty work that may arise
options.B: Spent on an unsanctioned work of the same section to avoid lapse of funds
options.C: Surrendered promptly through the prescribed budgetary exercise so that the funds can be allotted elsewhere
options.D: Adjusted against the departmental charges of another work

q: A division proposes to meet the cost of a new capital work by re-appropriating funds allotted for a work chargeable to Revenue, on the ground that both works are in the same section. The proposal is not in order because re-appropriation:

options.A: Is permissible only between two deposit works
options.B: Can be made only by the contractor executing the works
options.C: Requires no sanction when the two works are in the same section
options.D: Between Capital and Revenue heads is prohibited, the two classes of expenditure being distinct

q: At the final settlement of a contract, the contractor disputes the quantities of an item for which payment has been made in the running bills. The quantities payable are determined with reference to:

options.A: The entries of measurements recorded in the Measurement Book and accepted for the work
options.B: The quantities claimed in the contractor's own statement of work done
options.C: The quantities provided in the abstract estimate of the work
options.D: The quantities mentioned in the tender notice for the work

q: A contract is extended beyond its original completion date, but the bank guarantee furnished by the contractor towards performance guarantee is due to expire before the extended date. Before the guarantee expires, the Railway should:

options.A: Treat the guarantee as automatically extended for the extended period
options.B: Require the contractor to get the validity of the guarantee suitably extended, covering the extended period and the claim period
options.C: Return the guarantee and proceed without any security for the balance work
options.D: Recover the guarantee amount from the earnest money of other tenderers

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Performance Guarantee is furnished by the successful tenderer after the issue of the Letter of Acceptance.
2. Security Deposit is recovered from the contractor, ordinarily through deductions from his running bills, and is distinct from the Performance Guarantee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A buyer organisation proposes to procure a service available on the Government e-Marketplace and the value is beyond the limit up to which direct purchase on the portal is permitted. In such a case, the procurement on GeM is required to be made:

options.A: By nomination of a seller known to the buyer
options.B: Only through a works tender on IREPS
options.C: By obtaining the seller's quotation outside the portal and paying in cash
options.D: Through the competitive modes prescribed for the portal, such as bidding or reverse auction, or selection of the lowest offer through comparison, as applicable

q: A dispute under a works contract is taken up for conciliation under the contract conditions, but the conciliation proceedings end without any settlement between the parties. The next course open to the aggrieved party under the contract is to:

options.A: Invoke arbitration in accordance with the arbitration clause of the contract
options.B: Withhold the security deposit of the contractor permanently without further process
options.C: Place the dispute before the Tender Committee for its decision
options.D: Treat the contract as closed and write off all claims of both parties

q: A contract is terminated for the contractor's default and the balance work is got executed through another agency at higher rates. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting contractor as risk and cost is essentially:

options.A: The liquidated damages for the whole original completion period
options.B: The excess of the cost of executing the balance work through the new agency over the cost at which that balance work would have been executed under the original contract
options.C: The full value of the original contract, irrespective of the work already done
options.D: The amount of the performance guarantee furnished under the original contract

q: A work is completed and closed, but the staff specially engaged for its execution continues to be retained and their pay is proposed to be charged to the completed work. This is irregular because work-charged establishment:

options.A: Is a part of the permanent establishment of the division
options.B: Is provided by the contractor and paid for by him
options.C: Is sanctioned for the specific work and is to be discontinued when the work is completed, its cost being charged to that work
options.D: Can be charged to any work of the division after its engagement

q: An outside body which has deposited money for a deposit work withdraws its request before the work is taken up, after the Railways have incurred some expenditure on preparing the estimate and plans for it. The amount deposited by the body is dealt with by:

options.A: Forfeiting the entire deposit to the Railways
options.B: Crediting the entire deposit to the earnings of the Railways
options.C: Transferring the deposit to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Refunding the deposit after recovering the expenditure actually incurred by the Railways in connection with the proposed work

q: The maintenance and other charges payable by the owner of a private siding to the Railways are billed and watched for realisation by initially bringing them into account under the head:

options.A: Demands Recoverable
options.B: Stores Suspense
options.C: Traffic Suspense
options.D: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense

q: A licensee of railway land defaults in paying the licence fee and continues in occupation of the land after the licence has been terminated. In such a situation, the Railways can proceed against the occupant:

options.A: Only by requesting the licensee to vacate the land voluntarily
options.B: Under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971, treating the occupant as an unauthorised occupant of public premises
options.C: By adjusting the dues against the earnings of an unrelated work
options.D: Only after obtaining a decree from a civil court in every case

q: A railway executes a work for another Government department and recovers the cost of the work from that department. The departmental charges on such a work are:

options.A: Leviable only when the work is executed for a private party
options.B: Waived in all cases between Government departments
options.C: Leviable on the work in the same manner as on other works executed for outside bodies, to cover establishment and supervision costs
options.D: Credited to the contractor executing the work

q: A contractor has taken an advance against plant and machinery brought to the site and the advance still remains partly unrecovered. Until the advance is fully recovered, the plant and machinery against which it was granted:

options.A: Can be sold by the contractor to another contractor at his discretion
options.B: Become the property of the Railways permanently
options.C: Are transferred to the stores depot as railway stock
options.D: Are not to be removed from the site by the contractor without the permission of the Railway

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A secured advance is paid against the assessed value of durable materials actually brought to the site for incorporation in the work.
2. A secured advance, once paid, is not required to be adjusted and remains payable in addition to the value of the work done.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: On a work, the Railway failed to hand over a part of the site for several months and the contractor has claimed extension of the completion period on that account. While examining the claim, the entries in the Hindrance Register are relevant because they:

options.A: Show the rates quoted by the contractor for the items of the work
options.B: Record the hindrances met during execution, with their periods, which bear on the assessment of the delay
options.C: Record the measurements of the work done from time to time
options.D: Show the recoveries effected from the contractor's bills

q: During execution, the Engineer issues an instruction to the contractor at the site for a change in the manner of executing a portion of the work. To be effective and capable of being acted upon and verified later, such an instruction should be:

options.A: Conveyed only orally to the contractor's supervisor at the site
options.B: Recorded in the tender documents of another work in the section
options.C: Recorded in the Site Order Book maintained at the site and brought to the notice of the contractor
options.D: Communicated through the Accounts office at the time of the final bill

q: A portion of a work under execution is damaged by fire and the contractor receives money under the insurance policy taken for the work. Under the conditions of contract, the amount so received is required to be:

options.A: Retained by the contractor as compensation for his loss
options.B: Credited to the earnings of the Railways
options.C: Adjusted against the liquidated damages of the contract
options.D: Applied towards reinstating and making good the damaged work

q: Floods of an exceptional nature wash away a part of a work under execution and the contractor seeks relief under the force majeure provisions of the contract. For such relief to be considered, the contractor is ordinarily expected to:

options.A: Give notice of the event to the Railway within the time provided in the contract and take reasonable steps to mitigate the loss
options.B: Abandon the work immediately without informing the Railways
options.C: Claim payment for the entire contract value as compensation
options.D: Stop all correspondence and await the expiry of the contract period

q: Without obtaining any consent, a contractor sublets the whole of a railway work to another firm and himself withdraws from the site. On this coming to notice, the Railways may treat the unauthorised subletting as:

options.A: A normal arrangement requiring no action by the Railways
options.B: A breach of the conditions of contract, entailing action under the contract, including its determination
options.C: A matter between the contractor and the other firm only, with which the Railways have no concern
options.D: Grounds for increasing the rates payable under the contract

q: Samples of materials brought by a contractor are sent for testing and a lot is found not conforming to the specification. The cost of such testing, where the contract so provides, is borne by:

options.A: The Accounts office of the division
options.B: The tenderer who was second lowest in the tender
options.C: The contractor whose materials are tested
options.D: The stores depot of the Railway

q: After a contract for a station building is awarded, the Railways decide to add several additional structures and to change the design so fundamentally that the work bears little resemblance to the work tendered for. Such a far-reaching change is objectionable because it amounts to:

options.A: An ordinary deviation within the contract
options.B: A material alteration of the scope of the work
options.C: An extra item within the meaning of the contract
options.D: Vitiation of the contract, the work as altered being different in character from the work contracted for

q: The validity of tenders for a work is expiring and the Railways request all tenderers to extend it by a further period. One tenderer declines to extend the validity of his tender. In his case:

options.A: He ceases to be bound after the original validity period and is entitled to the refund of his earnest money
options.B: His earnest money is forfeited for refusing the extension
options.C: His tender is deemed to be extended indefinitely
options.D: He is debarred from all future tenders of the Railways

q: Negotiations held with the lowest tenderer for a work fail to bring his rates to a reasonable level. The proper course for the Railways thereafter is to:

options.A: Hold negotiations with the second lowest tenderer for the same work
options.B: Accept the rates of the lowest tenderer without recording any reasons
options.C: Reject the tenders and invite fresh tenders for the work
options.D: Direct the lowest tenderer to reduce his rates to the schedule rates

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where formation of a cartel among the tenderers for a work is reasonably suspected, the tender process need not be allowed to proceed as a genuine competition.
2. Suspected cartel formation among tenderers can be dealt with under the procurement rules, including rejection of the tenders concerned.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A work is awarded to a joint venture of two firms and a dispute later arises regarding the liability of the individual member firms towards the Railways for the obligations of the joint venture. Ordinarily, the member firms of the joint venture are:

options.A: Liable only in proportion to their shareholding, with no liability for each other's defaults
options.B: Not liable at all, the joint venture alone being answerable
options.C: Liable only up to the amount of earnest money furnished by them
options.D: Jointly and severally liable to the Railways for the obligations under the contract

q: In e-tendering for a work through IREPS, a tenderer asks how the earnest money for the tender is to be furnished. He is correctly advised that it is furnished:

options.A: Through the modes prescribed in the tender documents, such as online payment or bank guarantee/FDR
options.B: In cash only, at the Railway cash office
options.C: By a personal cheque drawn in favour of the Engineer
options.D: After the acceptance of his tender is communicated to him

q: Measurements recorded for a work are test-checked by the superior officer and a quantity is found to have been recorded and paid for in excess of the work actually executed. The excess payment so detected is dealt with by:

options.A: Ignoring it, as on-account payments cannot be corrected
options.B: Recovery or adjustment from the subsequent bills or other sums due to the contractor
options.C: Charging it to the contingencies of the estimate
options.D: Writing it off without the sanction of any authority

q: The expenditure booked in the accounts against a work does not agree with the expenditure shown in the Works Register maintained for that work. The difference is required to be:

options.A: Carried forward indefinitely as an unexplained balance
options.B: Adjusted by altering the entries in the Works Register without reference to the accounts
options.C: Charged to Miscellaneous Works Advances in all cases
options.D: Investigated and reconciled between the executive and accounts records, so that both show the same expenditure for the work

q: At the close of a financial year, work has been executed and measured on a sanctioned work but the contractor's bill for it has not been passed or paid. In order that the liability for the work done is reflected in the accounts of that year, the amount is:

options.A: Brought to account through the liability provisions maintained for works expenditure
options.B: Ignored, as no payment has actually been made during the year
options.C: Charged to the work of the succeeding year as fresh expenditure
options.D: Recovered from the contractor as an advance payment

q: On physical verification of the materials lying at the site of a work, the quantity of a material is found to be much less than the balance shown in the Material-at-Site account of the work. The shortage so found is required to be:

options.A: Written off automatically at the close of the work
options.B: Investigated, and adjusted in the accounts of the work under proper sanction after the responsibility and the correct accountal are determined
options.C: Charged to the contractor's earnest money in all cases
options.D: Shown as consumption on the work without any enquiry

q: The cost of a work is likely to exceed its sanctioned estimate, though there is no change in the scope or design of the work and the excess is due to a general rise in the prices of materials and labour. The situation is dealt with by preparing:

options.A: A supplementary estimate for the work
options.B: A completion report of the work
options.C: A revised estimate for sanction of the competent authority, explaining the excess over the sanctioned estimate
options.D: A fresh abstract estimate treating the work as a new work

q: An additional facility, not provided in the sanctioned estimate of a work, is executed during the progress of the work without obtaining any prior sanction for the change. Such execution is irregular because a material modification of a sanctioned work requires:

options.A: Only the approval of the contractor executing the work
options.B: Sanction only after the completion report of the work is prepared
options.C: The approval of the Tender Committee which dealt with the original tender
options.D: Prior sanction of the competent authority, with finance concurrence, before the modified work is executed

q: In a buyer organisation registered on the Government e-Marketplace, subordinate users with the roles of Buyer, Consignee and Paying Authority function on the portal under:

options.A: The primary user of the organisation, who creates and manages such user roles for the organisation
options.B: The seller who receives the orders of the organisation
options.C: The Railway Board, which creates every user of every organisation
options.D: The consignee of each order, who creates all other users

q: Goods ordered on the Government e-Marketplace have been received and accepted by the consignee, who has generated the Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate. Payment to the seller for the accepted supply is thereafter arranged by:

options.A: The contractor executing works in the same office
options.B: The Paying Authority of the buyer organisation, on the basis of the acceptance so recorded
options.C: The Tender Committee of the division
options.D: The seller himself, by debiting the buyer's account

q: An arbitral award in a works dispute has become final, no application for setting it aside having been made within the period allowed. The award is then enforceable:

options.A: Only after it is approved by the Railway Board
options.B: Only if the contractor gives his consent in writing
options.C: In the same manner as a decree of a court, in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
options.D: Only through a fresh arbitration on the same dispute

q: A party aggrieved by an arbitral award in a works dispute wishes to challenge it. Such a challenge by way of an application for setting aside the award can be made only:

options.A: On any ground of fact which the party considers unjust
options.B: Before the Tender Committee which dealt with the contract
options.C: By way of a regular appeal on the merits of the dispute
options.D: On the limited grounds specified in the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, within the period prescribed in that Act

q: In an EPC contract for a major work, the contractor claims payment on the ground that he has incurred expenditure on various items of the project. Payment under such a contract is ordinarily released:

options.A: In stages linked to the completion of the defined milestones or activities of the project, as provided in the contract
options.B: On the basis of item-wise measurements of every item executed, as in an item-rate contract
options.C: Only after the defect liability period of the whole project has expired
options.D: As a fixed monthly amount unrelated to the progress of the project

q: Under the annuity arrangement of a public-private partnership project, the demand and traffic risk of the project, that is, the risk that the actual usage of the facility may be less than expected, is borne by:

options.A: The private partner, who is paid only out of the user charges collected
options.B: The authority, the private partner being paid fixed annuity payments by the authority during the concession period
options.C: The lenders of the project alone
options.D: The users of the facility collectively

q: Vacant railway land identified for commercial development is entrusted to the Rail Land Development Authority. The development rights over such land are ordinarily awarded by the Authority:

options.A: By nomination to a developer of its choice
options.B: Only to the Railways' own production units
options.C: Through a competitive bidding process, the land being given on lease for development
options.D: By sale of the land outright to the developer

q: A way-leave permission has been granted to a party for laying a pipeline across railway land. The Railways later require the strip of land for their own operational purposes. In such a case, the permission:

options.A: Has become a permanent right of the party and cannot be disturbed
options.B: Can be withdrawn only on payment of the full market value of the land to the party
options.C: Entitles the party to ownership of an alternative strip of railway land
options.D: Being a bare permission creating no ownership or tenancy rights, can be terminated by the Railways in accordance with its terms, the party removing its installations

q: For an item of work for which no rate is available in the schedule of rates, the rate adopted in the estimate and used for evaluating the tenders is arrived at by:

options.A: Adopting the rate demanded by the lowest tenderer for that item
options.B: Analysis of rates, working out the cost of materials, labour, carriage and other charges involved in executing the item
options.C: Adopting the highest rate quoted in any tender received earlier
options.D: Leaving the rate blank in the estimate and fixing it after the work is done

q: An officer, who is competent to sanction expenditure on works, proposes to sanction a work the execution of which will directly benefit himself. The proposal offends against the canons of financial propriety because:

options.A: Works can be sanctioned only by the Railway Board in all cases
options.B: The sanctioning officer should not be a railway employee
options.C: All works benefiting any individual are prohibited in all circumstances
options.D: No authority should exercise its powers of sanctioning expenditure so as to benefit itself, directly or indirectly

q: For large works tenders covered by an Integrity Pact, the Independent External Monitors named in the pact are approached by a bidder principally in order to:

options.A: Obtain an extension of the date of submission of his tender
options.B: Lodge a complaint regarding any irregularity or lack of transparency noticed by him in the tender process
options.C: Get his rates certified as reasonable before submission of the tender
options.D: Seek exemption from furnishing the earnest money for the tender

q: A firm wishing to submit its tender for a railway work through the IREPS e-tendering portal is required, for authenticating and encrypting its electronic bid, to possess:

options.A: A valid Digital Signature Certificate of the prescribed class, obtained from a licensed certifying authority
options.B: A physical seal of the firm attested by a notary public
options.C: A user account on the Government e-Marketplace alone
options.D: A letter of authorisation issued by the tender inviting authority

q: In e-tendering through IREPS, a tenderer attempts to upload his bid a few minutes after the stipulated closing date and time for submission of tenders. The position in the system is that:

options.A: The bid is accepted, but is opened only after all timely bids have been opened
options.B: The bid is accepted on payment of a late-submission charge prescribed in the tender notice
options.C: The bid cannot be submitted, the portal not permitting submission of bids after the closing date and time
options.D: The bid is received in a separate folder and considered only if all timely bids are rejected

q: The eligibility conditions of a works tender require the tenderer to have completed, in the prescribed preceding period, a work of a 'similar nature'. This condition is intended to test:

options.A: The total turnover of the tenderer's firm from all kinds of business
options.B: The number of engineers on the permanent rolls of the tenderer's firm
options.C: The tenderer's ownership of plant and machinery required for the work
options.D: The tenderer's past experience of executing work of the same general character as the work tendered for

q: The authority competent to accept a tender is not in agreement with the recommendation made by the Tender Committee in respect of that tender. The correct course for the accepting authority is to:

options.A: Record its own reasons in writing for differing from the recommendation and decide the tender accordingly, referring the matter to the next higher authority where so required
options.B: Alter the recommendation of the Committee in the Committee's minutes itself
options.C: Accept the tender recommended by the Committee without recording any reasons, the recommendation being binding on it
options.D: Direct the Committee to meet again and repeat its deliberations until it recommends what the accepting authority desires

q: An officer nominated as a member of the Tender Committee for a work finds that one of the tenderers for the work is a close relation of his. The proper course for the officer is to:

options.A: Disclose the relationship and keep himself away from the deliberations and recommendation of the Committee in that tender
options.B: Continue as a member, but abstain from signing the comparative statement of tenders
options.C: Continue as a member, since the Committee decides collectively and no individual responsibility arises
options.D: Inform the tenderer relation to withdraw his tender from the competition

q: Before an order banning business dealings with a contractor is issued on the ground of his serious defaults in railway works, the procedure ordinarily requires that:

options.A: The contractor's earnest money for all future tenders be enhanced
options.B: The contractor be blacklisted first and heard only after the order takes effect
options.C: The contractor be given an opportunity, by way of a show-cause notice, to represent against the proposed banning
options.D: The consent of all the tenderers who competed with him be obtained

q: A tenderer for a work is found to have directly approached officers connected with the tender, offering inducements to secure acceptance of his tender. Such canvassing on the part of the tenderer renders his tender:

options.A: Eligible for acceptance at a reduced rate, as a penalty
options.B: Liable to be rejected, apart from any other action that may be taken against him
options.C: Eligible only for works of a smaller value in future
options.D: Unaffected, canvassing having no bearing on the tender conditions

q: In a works tender invited under the two-packet system, the technical packet of a tenderer is evaluated and found not to meet the eligibility conditions of the tender. His financial packet is then:

options.A: Opened along with the financial packets of the eligible tenderers, but his rates are kept aside
options.B: Opened only for the purpose of preparing the comparative statement
options.C: Returned to him after the work has been completed by another contractor
options.D: Not opened at all, only the financial packets of the tenderers found technically eligible being opened

q: A contract for the housekeeping and facility-management services of an office complex, involving the deployment of manpower and the rendering of services over a period, is governed by:

options.A: The General Conditions of Contract for Works, since the services are rendered at a work site
options.B: The Indian Railway Stores Code, since consumables are used in the services
options.C: The General Conditions of Contract for Services, which are distinct from the GCC for Works
options.D: The conditions of the contractor's licence under the Contract Labour Act alone

q: Before placing an order for goods or services on the Government e-Marketplace, the buyer is required to satisfy himself and certify, in accordance with the procurement rules, that:

options.A: The seller selected is the oldest registered seller in that product category
options.B: The price of the selected offer is reasonable, with reference to the prevailing market price, last purchase price and other available offers
options.C: The goods will be consumed before the end of the financial year in every case
options.D: No other buyer organisation has purchased the same item in that year

q: While procuring a requirement through the Government e-Marketplace or otherwise, the specifications of the item framed by the buyer should ordinarily be:

options.A: Generic and functional in character, so as to permit fair competition among sellers, and not tailored to the product of a particular brand or seller without justification
options.B: Copied from the catalogue of the preferred seller, so that only his product matches them
options.C: Kept deliberately vague, so that any product offered can be accepted
options.D: Framed afresh for each purchase, without reference to the standards prescribed for the item

q: The bills arising out of procurements made through the Government e-Marketplace are processed for payment on the Railways through:

options.A: A separate manual register maintained by the consignee
options.B: The seller's own accounting software, to which the Railways have no access
options.C: Cash payment by the consignee on delivery of the goods
options.D: The GeM portal's billing facility, which is linked with the Railways' IPAS system for passing and payment of the bills

q: In preparing the estimate for a renewal work, such as the complete renewal of a section of track, a provision is made on the credit side of the estimate in respect of:

options.A: The liquidated damages expected to be recovered from the contractor
options.B: The departmental charges leviable on the work
options.C: The value of the serviceable and scrap materials expected to be released from the existing asset on its renewal
options.D: The interest payable on the capital cost of the work

q: In the course of the Finance vetting of a detailed estimate of a work, the scrutiny of the Finance branch is directed principally to:

options.A: Re-designing the work so as to reduce its technical specifications
options.B: Selecting the contractor by whom the work is to be executed
options.C: The correctness of the allocation, the availability of funds, the rates adopted and the financial propriety of the proposal, and not to the technical design of the work, which is the responsibility of the executive
options.D: Fixing the date by which the contractor must complete the work

q: A traffic survey carried out in connection with a proposed new railway line is concerned principally with:

options.A: Assessing the volume and nature of the traffic likely to be carried by the proposed line and the earnings expected from it, so as to judge its remunerativeness
options.B: Counting the trains running on the adjoining existing lines on a single day
options.C: Fixing the fares and freight rates to be charged on the proposed line
options.D: Selecting the contractor for the construction of the line

q: The final location survey of a proposed new railway line, as the last stage of the survey work, results in:

options.A: A rough comparison of the alternative routes considered for the line
options.B: The preparation of only a traffic forecast for the line
options.C: The issue of tenders for the earthwork of the line
options.D: The alignment of the line being finally fixed and pegged on the ground, with the detailed plans and land-acquisition proposals prepared on that basis

q: Against an itemised work shown in the Pink Book, the 'outlay' provided for a particular year represents:

options.A: The total sanctioned cost of the work from its commencement to its completion
options.B: The amount expected to be spent on the work during that year, the balance of its cost being provided in the subsequent years
options.C: The amount of liabilities outstanding against the work at the end of the year
options.D: The value of the materials lying at the site of the work

q: A Detailed Project Report prepared for a major railway project ordinarily brings out, among other things:

options.A: Only the names of the officers who will supervise the project
options.B: The final bill of a similar project executed in an earlier year
options.C: The scope and cost estimates of the project, the traffic projections for it and the result of its financial appraisal
options.D: The text of the tender conditions to be applied to all works of the project

q: Where a material modification of a sanctioned work becomes necessary, the modified work requires the sanction of:

options.A: The authority competent to sanction the work as so modified, obtained before the modified portion is executed
options.B: The contractor executing the work, by way of his written consent alone
options.C: The sectional officer supervising the work, irrespective of the cost involved
options.D: No authority, a material modification being covered by the original sanction in all cases

q: In working out the total capital cost of a project for the purpose of its financial appraisal, the interest payable on the capital locked up during the period of construction of the project is:

options.A: Ignored altogether, interest having no relation to a project under construction
options.B: Treated as part of the cost of the project, as interest during construction
options.C: Charged to the revenue account of the year in which the survey is made
options.D: Recovered from the contractor who will execute the project

q: Corrections made in the entries of a Measurement Book, which is an important original record of the work done, are required to be:

options.A: Made by erasing the original entry completely, so that the corrected figure alone is visible
options.B: Made by the contractor, without reference to the official who recorded the measurements
options.C: Carried out on a separate loose sheet attached to the book at the end of the work
options.D: Effected by scoring out the wrong entry and writing the correct one, the correction being attested by the official making it

q: The signature of the contractor, or of his authorised representative, taken on the Measurement Book at the time the measurements are recorded signifies:

options.A: His acceptance of the measurements recorded therein
options.B: His agreement to execute extra items free of charge
options.C: His undertaking to complete the work before the stipulated date
options.D: His consent to the levy of liquidated damages for past delays

q: Materials brought to the site by a contractor for incorporation in a work are to be used on the work only after:

options.A: The final bill of the work has been prepared
options.B: The contractor has been paid a secured advance against the whole lot
options.C: They have been inspected and approved by the Engineer as conforming to the specifications of the contract
options.D: The maintenance period of the work has commenced

q: The Engineer directs the contractor, in writing, to suspend the progress of a portion of the work for reasons of safety of the running line. The contractor is thereafter to resume that portion of the work:

options.A: At his own convenience, whenever his labour becomes available
options.B: Only after the final bill of the work is passed
options.C: After obtaining a fresh contract for that portion
options.D: On receiving the instructions of the Engineer to resume the work

q: A works contractor owes money to the Railways on account of the cost of departmental materials supplied to him and other dues under a completed contract, while amounts are payable to him under another contract with the Railways. Under the conditions of contract, the dues owed by him may be recovered by the Railways:

options.A: Only by filing a suit against him in a civil court
options.B: From the sums payable to him under that other contract as well, by way of set-off
options.C: Only from the earnest money furnished by him for future tenders
options.D: Only after the expiry of the maintenance period of the other contract

q: A works contract is foreclosed by the Railways for reasons unconnected with any default of the contractor, a part of the work remaining unexecuted. In the settlement of such a foreclosed contract, the contractor is ordinarily entitled to:

options.A: Payment for the work actually executed and for the materials taken over, but not to compensation for the profit he might have earned on the unexecuted portion
options.B: The full contract value, as if the whole work had been executed by him
options.C: Payment only of the earnest money furnished by him
options.D: Compensation equal to the liquidated damages prescribed in the contract

q: Under the indemnity provisions of a works contract, the contractor is bound to indemnify the Railways against:

options.A: The losses suffered by the Railways on the working of the section as a whole
options.B: The expenditure incurred by the Railways on the maintenance of the completed work
options.C: Claims, damages and liabilities arising out of the acts and operations of the contractor in the execution of the work
options.D: The cost of the departmental establishment supervising the work

q: During the execution of a work, the Engineer finds a workman or supervisor employed by the contractor to be incompetent or guilty of misconduct at the site. Under the conditions of contract, the Engineer may:

options.A: Impose a departmental penalty on the person, as if he were a railway servant
options.B: Require the contractor to remove that person from the work and not to re-employ him on it without permission
options.C: Suspend the contractor's payments for the whole work indefinitely
options.D: Direct the contractor to dismiss the person from his employment altogether

q: A dispute has arisen between a works contractor and the Railways and the contractor has invoked the dispute-resolution provisions of the contract. Pending the settlement of that dispute, the position under the conditions of contract is that:

options.A: The contractor may stop all work on the contract until the dispute is decided in his favour
options.B: The work under the contract stands automatically foreclosed
options.C: The Railways may withhold even the admitted amounts payable to the contractor
options.D: The contractor is to continue the work in accordance with the contract and the instructions of the Engineer, unless otherwise directed
